title: Sharing, federation and interoperability
summary: Copy, governed share, federation or clean room: what moves, who enforces, who pays, how revocation works, how fresh the view is and how each fails, with OpenSharing, Lakehouse Federation, UniForm and Iceberg catalogs taken down to their request paths.
outcomes: Compare copy, governed share, federation and clean room on movement, enforcement, cost in kind, revocation, freshness and failure.
Explain OpenSharing's objects, recipient modes, credentials and read path without renaming Delta Sharing protocol identifiers.
Choose between ingestion and access-in-place and read the evidence that a federated filter was pushed down.
Explain how UniForm, Iceberg REST catalogs and clean rooms change what an outside party can read, and rehearse a revocation.
startingAssumptions: Unity Catalog names, grants and least-privilege scope from the governance module are familiar.
A Delta table is Parquet files plus a transaction log whose versions are snapshots, as taught in the Delta module.
editorialRationale: Sharing decisions fail when a product name stands in for a mechanism, so the module first puts copy, share and federation on one diagram of movement, enforcement and ownership, then takes the governed share down to its objects, recipient modes, credentials and request path, where freshness and the revocation tail become visible. Federation and pushdown follow, with ingestion as the alternative, then open table formats and catalog interoperability for engines outside Databricks, then clean rooms for the case where neither party may see rows. It closes on the same six questions the sharing and federation field guide uses. Protocol and API facts come from primary texts read in this build (the Delta Sharing protocol, the Databricks SDK's API reference, the Delta Lake UniForm documentation and the Iceberg REST specification); Databricks pages that could not be re-read are marked as such.

sources.title: Delta Sharing Protocol
sources.context: Open protocol specification, main branch as fetched 2026-09-23; applies to any Delta Sharing server and client, including Databricks'.
sources.caveat: A specification states what servers and clients may do; a given server, including Databricks', may implement optional fields such as URL expiration timestamps differently. Pin a commit when citing exact behaviour.
sources.reviewedEvidence: Read in this build on 2026-09-23 from the raw file (raw.githubusercontent.com, HTTP 200; SHA-256 ff2631fb8177fb8acd9cc448db3c5179e1df6e0e0cf5b933904a39ffd457535c): the Overview, Concepts, Access Modes, Query Table Version, Read Data from a Table (request body and File), Read Change Data Feed, Generate Temporary Table Credential, Capabilities Header and Profile File Format sections. Passage relied on: a share groups schemas and tables for recipients and a table is a Delta table or a view on one; a recipient is a principal holding a bearer token, and every REST API uses bearer tokens; Read Data from a Table returns files as HTTPS URLs the client reads directly, with an optional expirationTimestamp, or, with directory-based access, temporary read-only credentials with an expirationTime; predicateHints, jsonPredicateHints and limitHint are best effort and the client must apply them itself; version and timestamp reads need history sharing; a client may cache file content by file id and use Query Table Version to detect a stale cache; the delta response format enables reading tables with minReaderVersion above 1, such as those with deletion vectors or column mapping, and a client that did not request it must fail if the server answers in it; the profile file holds shareCredentialsVersion, endpoint, bearerToken and an optional expirationTime whose absence means the token can be seen as never expiring.

claims.description: Databricks' current documentation titles its sharing overview 'What is OpenSharing?', and the historical delta-sharing documentation URL leads there; the open protocol specification is titled Delta Sharing Protocol; connectors read shares through the deltaSharing Spark format and the delta_sharing Python package; the Databricks API names the resources shares, recipients and providers and still describes a delta sharing authentication type.
claims.context: Naming at documentation, protocol, connector and API layers; checked 2026-09-20 (page record) and 2026-09-23 (primary texts).

claims.description: In the Delta Sharing protocol every REST call carries a bearer token; a read returns the table's files as HTTPS URLs that the client downloads directly, each optionally with an expiration timestamp, or temporary read-only credentials for the table directory; predicate and limit hints are best effort and the client must apply them; older versions or timestamps are served only with history sharing; clients may cache files by id and check the table version to detect staleness; the delta response format enables reading tables with advanced reader features, and a client that did not request it must fail if the server answers in it.
claims.context: Open protocol specification, main branch read 2026-09-23.

claims.description: A recipient's profile file contains shareCredentialsVersion, the sharing server endpoint, a bearer token and an optional expirationTime, and a token without expirationTime can be seen as never expiring; connectors address a shared table as the profile path followed by '#' and share, schema and table names.
claims.context: Protocol profile format and connector README, read 2026-09-23.

claims.description: Databricks-to-Databricks recipients are created from the recipient's sharing identifier (cloud:region:metastore-uuid) and exchange no token; open-sharing recipients download a credential file once from an activation link or authenticate with OIDC federation; recipients can carry an IP access list and a token expiry; rotate_token can only shorten the existing token's expiry and 0 expires it at once; creating a recipient needs CREATE_RECIPIENT.
claims.context: Databricks API reference in SDK 0.141.0; feature status per workspace to be verified.

claims.description: A share is a container of existing metastore objects, optionally under aliases; object types in the API include tables, views, materialized views, streaming tables, foreign tables, volumes, models, functions and notebook files; the share owner must keep SELECT on each shared table indefinitely and a group owner is advised; history sharing is disabled unless enabled; start_version sets the lowest queryable version; granting needs USE_SHARE and SET_SHARE_PERMISSION or ownership, and revoking a recipient needs no additional privilege; a recipient's Delta Sharing catalog is created from a provider name and share name.
claims.context: Databricks API reference in SDK 0.141.0; which types a recipient type can read is to be verified.

claims.description: Lakehouse Federation uses a Unity Catalog connection holding an external source's options and credentials and a foreign catalog created from that connection; query federation pushes work to the remote database while catalog federation reads external tables from object storage with Databricks compute; the overview describes both as read-only; connection types in the API include PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Oracle, Teradata, Hive metastore and AWS Glue, governed by CREATE CONNECTION, USE CONNECTION and CREATE FOREIGN CATALOG.
claims.context: Federation overview as reviewed 2026-09-19 and API enums read 2026-09-23; connector support to be verified per source.

claims.description: In Lakehouse Federation some predicates push down to the source while others remain local; EXPLAIN FORMATTED exposes the remote query, with an adaptive-execution caveat; JDBC fetchSize controls rows per batch, not parallelism.

Lakeflow Connect provides managed ingestion connectors in categories including change-data-capture database ingestion, files, streaming and query-based ingestion, with service models and source support that differ by connector.

UniForm lets Iceberg clients read a Delta table from the same Parquet files by generating Iceberg metadata asynchronously after each Delta commit, possibly bundling commits; converted_delta_version records the Delta version reflected; it is enabled by delta.enableIcebergCompatV2 and delta.universalFormat.enabledFormats, requires column mapping and irreversible protocol upgrades, is read-only for Iceberg clients, and in open-source Delta does not work with deletion vectors.
claims.context: Open-source Delta Lake documentation and protocol read 2026-09-23; Databricks-specific requirements to be verified.

claims.description: Iceberg REST catalog clients call /v1/config, then load a table to receive its metadata location and configuration, and may request vended credentials or remote signing for storage access; the open-source Unity Catalog states compatibility with the Iceberg REST catalog API and the Hive metastore API.
claims.context: Iceberg REST OpenAPI specification and Unity Catalog OSS README read 2026-09-23.

claims.description: Unity Catalog's temporary table credentials are short-lived, downscoped storage credentials (STS on AWS, SAS on Azure, OAuth on Google Cloud); issuing them requires a metastore admin to enable the external access flag, off by default, and the catalog owner to grant EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA, which schema ownership and ALL PRIVILEGES do not include.
claims.context: Databricks API reference in SDK 0.141.0; endpoint paths for Iceberg clients to be verified on the current page.

claims.description: A Databricks clean room uses Delta Sharing and serverless compute so parties work together without direct access to each other's data; collaborators are identified by Unity Catalog global metastore identifiers; assets are tables, views, volumes, foreign tables, notebooks and JAR analyses; notebooks carry APPROVED, PENDING or REJECTED reviews and a list of collaborators allowed to run them; results go to an output catalog; the owner must keep privileges on assets; a deleted clean room remains in other collaborators' metastores in a deleted state.
claims.context: Databricks API reference in SDK 0.141.0; availability by cloud, region and billing to be verified.

claims.description: Recipients can read a shared table's change data feed between versions or timestamps, with _change_type, _commit_version and _commit_timestamp columns, when the provider enables change data feed on the shared object; start_version bounds how far back they may go; the Python connector exposes load_table_changes_as_pandas.
claims.context: Protocol, connector README and API reference read 2026-09-23.

claims.description: Recipient federation policies let non-Databricks recipients authenticate with short-lived OIDC tokens issued by their own identity provider, validated by claims set on the recipient, for user-to-machine and machine-to-machine flows, without static credentials.

A shared object's partition value can refer to a recipient property key instead of a literal value, and recipients carry key-value properties, so one shared table can expose different partitions to different recipients.
claims.context: PartitionValue and RecipientInfo data classes in SDK 0.141.0.

claims.description: The protocol defines URL-based access, where the server lists pre-signed file URLs, and directory-based access, where it issues temporary read-only cloud credentials for the table root with an expiration time; table metadata lists supported accessModes, and a client supporting only URLs must fail on a directory-only table.
claims.context: Protocol access modes and Generate Temporary Table Credential sections read 2026-09-23.

claims.description: Original SpicyBrain comparison method, decision tables, credential and rehearsal practices and thresholds for sharing, federation and interoperability; not a Databricks runbook or policy.
claims.context: Independent curriculum; adapt to the actual agreement, security review and current documentation.

claims.description: Cinderline Components, Halvern Coatings, Orvane Castings, Pellmark Polymers, their tables, shares, recipients, identifiers, timings, row counts and outcomes are synthetic teaching records.
claims.context: No share, recipient, connection, clean room or table was created, read or tested; no price or measured figure is implied.

concepts.definition: One of the ways another party reaches data: a delivered copy, a governed share read in place, a federated query against the source, or a clean room that shares computation.
concepts.example: Cinderline's weekly CSV to Halvern is a copy; its view read through a recipient is a governed share.

concepts.definition: Databricks' current documentation name for its product family that shares data and AI assets with other organizations, built on the open Delta Sharing protocol whose identifiers keep their original spelling.
concepts.example: Cinderline manages its share with OpenSharing, while Halvern's code still calls format('deltaSharing').

concepts.definition: A named container in the provider's metastore listing tables, views and other objects exposed to recipients, optionally under aliases.
concepts.example: halvern_line2_quality lists one view of line 2 coated-part defects.

concepts.definition: The object representing another organization that may read shares, carrying its authentication type, credentials or sharing identifier, and access restrictions.
concepts.example: halvern_coatings is an open-sharing recipient with a token expiry and an IP access list.

concepts.definition: Sharing to a recipient that has a Unity Catalog-enabled workspace, identified by its sharing identifier instead of a token.
concepts.example: Pellmark sends aws:eu-west-1 plus its metastore UUID, and its admin creates a catalog from Cinderline's share.

concepts.definition: Sharing to a recipient without a Unity Catalog workspace, authenticated by a bearer-token credential file or by OIDC federation.
concepts.example: Halvern downloads its credential file once from an activation link.

concepts.definition: A JSON profile holding shareCredentialsVersion, the sharing server endpoint, a bearer token and an optional expirationTime.
concepts.example: Halvern's nightly job reads its profile from a secret store before loading the shared view.

concepts.definition: A short-lived HTTPS link to one data file, issued by the sharing server so the client downloads directly from the provider's storage until it expires.
concepts.example: Halvern's 13:58 query received file URLs that expired later that hour.

concepts.definition: How far the version a reader works from trails the source's latest committed version at the moment it is used.
concepts.example: A DataFrame read at version 42 is stale once Cinderline commits version 43.

concepts.definition: A per-object share setting, disabled by default, that lets recipients query earlier versions or timestamps of a shared table.
concepts.example: Pellmark can compare today with last Tuesday only because history sharing is enabled.

concepts.definition: Removing a recipient's ability to make future reads by removing its grant, deleting it or expiring its token; bytes already delivered are not recalled.
concepts.example: Cinderline revokes at 14:00, Halvern's 14:03 query fails, and its saved extract remains.

concepts.definition: Querying an external database or catalog in place through a Unity Catalog connection and foreign catalog, without ingesting it.
concepts.example: Cinderline's analysts query MES work orders through the foreign catalog mes.

concepts.definition: A Unity Catalog catalog that mirrors one external database through a connection, so its tables are granted and queried with three-part names.
concepts.example: SELECT order_id FROM mes.public.work_orders reads the MES database in place.

concepts.definition: Translating filters, projections and limits into the query sent to an external source so fewer rows cross the network.
concepts.example: A pushed order_date filter moved 1,840 rows instead of 2.4 million.

concepts.definition: Reading data where it lives at query time, through a share or federation, instead of ingesting a copy into your own tables.
concepts.example: An engineer checks today's work orders through the foreign catalog rather than waiting for tonight's ingest.

concepts.definition: A Delta Lake table setting that also generates Apache Iceberg (or Hudi) metadata for the same Parquet files so other engines can read the table.
concepts.example: quality.gold.defects shows converted_delta_version 12 once the Iceberg conversion finishes.

concepts.definition: An open HTTP API through which Iceberg engines get catalog configuration, load table metadata and optionally receive vended storage credentials.
concepts.example: An open-source Spark job calls /v1/config, then loads quality.gold.defects.

concepts.definition: A catalog issuing short-lived, downscoped storage credentials for one table to an authorized engine outside the platform.
concepts.example: Unity Catalog vends credentials for quality.gold.defects only after EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA is granted.

concepts.definition: A shared environment where collaborators add data and reviewed code, run it on serverless compute and take away only its outputs, without direct access to each other's data.
concepts.example: Two companies correlate warranty returns with compound batches and receive only monthly aggregates.

concepts.definition: Reading a shared table's row-level changes between two versions or timestamps instead of re-reading the whole table.
concepts.example: Halvern's nightly job reads changes from version 42 to 45.

concepts.definition: Recipient authentication in which the recipient's identity provider issues short-lived tokens that a federation policy on the recipient validates.
concepts.example: Orvane's nightly job signs in through its own identity provider, with no credential file.

concepts.definition: A share partition specification that compares a partition column with a property of the reading recipient instead of a fixed value.
concepts.example: supplier_id = 'halvern' on Halvern's recipient exposes only Halvern's partitions.

concepts.definition: The two protocol ways to read a shared table: per-file pre-signed URLs, or temporary credentials for the table's directory.
concepts.example: A directory-only table fails for a client that supports only URLs.
